en: n. a sudden period of economic growth; a deep loud sound; a long pole that holds a microphone or sail; vi. to grow quickly in a successful way; to make a deep loud sound; vt. to cause something to grow or increase quickly
ex: The city experienced an economic boom in the 1990s.
這座城市在 1990 年代經歷了經濟繁榮。

en: n. a person whose job is to manage or control an organization or institution; a person who manages the legal affairs of a dead person's property; a person who administers something
ex: She is the administrator of the hospital.
她是這家醫院的行政主管。

en: a. (of a disease) easily passed from one person to another by touch or contact; (of a feeling) easily spreading from one person to another; spreading quickly
ex: The flu is a highly contagious disease.
流感是高度傳染性的疾病。

en: n. a supply of goods that a shop has for sale; the shares of a company; a liquid made by boiling meat or vegetables, used as a base for soups; the animals kept on a farm; vt. to keep a supply of something in a shop; vi. to store goods for future use
ex: The store has a large stock of winter clothes.
這家店有大量冬季服飾的庫存。

en: n. the leader of the government in some countries; the head of a government, especially a prime minister; a. first in importance, rank or position; best of its kind
ex: The premier met with other leaders at the summit.
總理在高峰會上與其他領袖會面。

en: n. a place where many people go for a holiday; a course of action that you take when other things have failed; the act of going to someone or something for help; vi. to use something or do something that you do not like because there is no other choice
ex: They spent a week at a seaside resort.
他們在海濱度假勝地待了一星期。

en: n. a person who believes in democracy; a member of the Democratic Party in the United States; a person who supports equal rights and the rule of the people
ex: He is a lifelong democrat who always votes in elections.
他是終身的民主主義者，每次選舉都投票。

en: vi. to shake slightly because you are cold, excited, nervous or afraid; to move quickly with small movements; n. a slight shaking movement; a case for carrying arrows; vt. to make something shake slightly
ex: Her voice quivered with emotion.
她的聲音因情緒激動而顫抖。

en: n. a severe emotional shock that has a lasting effect on someone; a serious physical injury; an upsetting experience that causes long-term emotional damage
ex: The soldiers suffered deep trauma from the war.
士兵們因戰爭而遭受深刻的創傷。

en: vi. to have the right to do something because you have met certain conditions; to be allowed to take part in a competition; vt. to give someone the necessary qualifications; to add something to a statement to limit its meaning
ex: She qualified for the Olympics after winning the race.
她贏得比賽後取得了奧運資格。

en: a. working and ready to be used; relating to the way a business or system works; ready to carry out its function; relating to the actions of military forces
ex: The new factory will be fully operational next month.
新工廠將在下個月全面運轉。

en: n. a person who has a lot of knowledge and skill in a particular subject; a doctor who treats a particular type of disease; a. relating to a particular subject or activity; having special skills
ex: She is a specialist in heart disease.
她是心臟疾病方面的專科醫生。

en: n. the feeling that someone or something is stupid and not worth respecting; a lack of respect for something; the state of being despised; (legal) disobedience to a court
ex: He looked at the cheater with contempt.
他以輕蔑的眼神看著作弊者。

en: n. a task that you have to do regularly, especially around the house; an unpleasant but necessary job; a small job; (British, old use) a boring job
ex: My brother and I share the household chores.
我和哥哥分擔家務。

en: n. the ability to change or be changed easily; the ability to bend easily without breaking; willingness to change to suit new situations
ex: The job offers a lot of flexibility in working hours.
這份工作在工作時間上很有彈性。

en: n. a particular way of thinking about something; the way that objects appear to be different in size and distance from where you stand; a sense of what is important in life; a. (of a drawing) giving the effect of distance
ex: Try to look at the problem from another perspective.
試著從另一個角度看這個問題。

en: n. a perfectly round solid object like a ball; an area of activity, interest or influence; a range of social status; vt. to form into a ball; to enclose something in a ball
ex: The moon is a sphere that orbits the Earth.
月球是繞著地球運行的球體。

en: n. something that is left to someone by a person who has died; something that remains from an earlier time; the effects of something that happened in the past; money or property left in a will
ex: The great artist left a rich cultural legacy.
那位大藝術家留下了豐富的文化遺產。

en: a. the only one; belonging to only one person or group; n. the flat bottom of the foot or shoe; a type of flatfish; vt. to put a new bottom on a shoe
ex: She is the sole survivor of the plane crash.
她是那場空難唯一的倖存者。

en: n. a sports or other competition in which many players or teams take part, and the winners continue to the next round; a series of contests; (historic) a medieval event in which knights fought each other
ex: The tennis tournament attracts players from around the world.
這場網球錦標賽吸引了世界各地的選手。

en: n. an important discovery or development that helps to solve a problem; a sudden advance in a difficult process; the act of breaking through a barrier or a defense
ex: Scientists announced a major breakthrough in cancer research.
科學家宣布了癌症研究的重大突破。

en: n. a serious argument or fight between people or groups; a face-to-face meeting in which people disagree or fight; the act of facing something difficult; a face-to-face meeting of witnesses in a court
ex: There was a confrontation between the police and the protesters.
警察與抗議者之間發生了對峙。

en: n. a group of ordinary people who listen to the evidence in a court case and decide whether someone is guilty; a group of people who judge a competition; a. (nautical) makeshift or temporary
ex: The jury found the defendant not guilty.
陪審團裁定被告無罪。

en: a. parallel to the ground or horizon; flat and level; (of a business structure) having few levels of management; (of a line) running from side to side; n. a line or plane that is parallel to the ground
ex: Draw a horizontal line across the middle of the page.
在頁面中間畫一條水平線。

en: n. the quality of being able to notice and understand other people's feelings; the quality of reacting quickly or strongly to something; the ability of an instrument to detect small changes; the quality of being easily hurt or upset
ex: The teacher showed great sensitivity to the students' needs.
老師對學生的需求表現出高度的敏感度。

en: n. a straight line that goes from one side of a circle to the other through the center; the length of this line; the width of a round object
ex: The tree trunk is one meter in diameter.
這棵樹的樹幹直徑一公尺。

en: a. able to speak well and persuade people; showing strong feeling in a clear way; speaking in a fluent and expressive way; (of something) clearly expressing a feeling
ex: She gave an eloquent speech that moved the audience.
她發表了一場打動觀眾的雄辯演說。

en: n. a statement that makes something seem better, worse, larger or more important than it really is; the act of overstating something; an example of overstating
ex: It is no exaggeration to say that he is a genius.
說他是天才一點也不誇張。

en: n. the activity or profession of collecting, writing and publishing news; the work of journalists; newspapers and magazines in general; the style of writing used in newspapers
ex: She is studying journalism at university.
她在大學主修新聞學。

en: n. a large and important Christian church, especially the main church of a particular area; a large church with a bishop; a. relating to a cathedral
ex: Thousands of tourists visit the famous cathedral every year.
每年有數千名遊客參觀這座著名的大教堂。

en: n. a product or raw material that can be bought and sold; something useful or valuable; a product that is traded on a market; something that is useful
ex: Oil and gold are important commodities in world trade.
石油和黃金是世界貿易中重要的商品。

en: vt. to make a series of short loud sounds; to make someone feel nervous or worried; vi. to make short loud sounds; to talk quickly and at length; n. a series of short loud sounds; a baby's toy that makes a noise when shaken
ex: The wind rattled the windows all night.
風整夜吹得窗戶嘎嘎作響。

en: vt. to make something easier or possible; to help a process or action happen more smoothly; to help a group of people to discuss something; to make progress easier
ex: The new software facilitates communication between teams.
新軟體促進了團隊之間的溝通。

en: a. different from what is usual, normal or expected; (of a medical condition) not normal; (of behavior) unusual in a way that is strange or worrying; n. a person or thing that is unusual
ex: The test results showed abnormal levels of sugar in his blood.
檢驗結果顯示他血液中的糖分異常。

en: n. a business deal in which something is bought or sold; the act of buying or selling something; a business agreement; (plural) official records of the meetings of an organization
ex: The bank recorded every transaction made on the account.
銀行記錄了帳戶上的每一筆交易。

en: n. a plant with strong-smelling leaves used for flavoring food and drinks; a sweet with a strong fresh flavor; a place where coins are made; a large amount of money; vt. to make coins; to invent something new
ex: She added fresh mint leaves to her tea.
她在茶裡加了新鮮的薄荷葉。

en: vi. to behave in the way that most people expect you to behave; to obey a rule or law; to be similar to something; vt. to make something agree with or match something else
ex: All students must conform to the school rules.
所有學生都必須遵守校規。

en: n. an amount of money you pay regularly for insurance; an extra amount of money paid for something; a reward; a. of high quality; costing more than usual
ex: The insurance premium goes up every year.
保險費每年都在上漲。

en: n. a powerful drug that is made from the leaves of a South American plant and is illegal in most countries; a drug used as a local anesthetic; a drug that gives a person a temporary feeling of energy
ex: The police seized a large amount of cocaine at the airport.
警方在機場查獲大量古柯鹼。

en: n. a new idea, method or invention; the act of introducing new things; something new and different; the process of making changes
ex: The company is known for its innovation in design.
公司以設計創新聞名。
